notes.TorusEuler.wavePotential_zero_of_profile: If the input profile is zero at every phase at a fixed label, its vector potential is zero there as well. This is the first support step after (3.6): integration in phase does not spread a profile to new particle labels. Locality of the spatial curl then supplies the corresponding support statement for the divergence correction.
notes.TorusEuler.wavePressureCoefficient: The coefficient is $2\widetilde\chi g\langle\kappa,M\mathbf a\rangle/|\kappa|^2$ for a nonzero phase gradient $\kappa$. At the centre, with cutoff equal to one, its normalization gives the relation between $p_{\rm w}$ and $\nu_+$ in §2.2.4. The formula itself imposes no sign; pressure positivity uses the coupling bound and the nonnegative cutoff.
notes.TorusEuler.wavePressureCoefficient_cente: For nonzero phase gradient and amplitude, the signed rank-one pressure tensor can be written in the unit wave direction with coefficient $-2\widetilde\chi g|\mathbf a||\kappa|\nu_+$. This is the tensor form of the normalization behind the scalar pressure identity in §2.2.4. The result is algebraic and does not assume that the coupling is positive.
notes.TorusEuler.wavePressureCoefficient_mul_n: If $\kappa\ne0$, the cutoff lies in $[0,1]$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge0$, then $c_{\mathbf a}\ge0$ and $c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2\le2|\kappa||M||\mathbf a|$. In Lemma 5.9 the cutoff is $\widetilde\chi g$ and the coupling supplies the sign. Together with the lower bound on $F_h^{\prime}$, this controls the leading pressure tensor from above.
notes.TorusEuler.wavePressurePrimitive: This defines $P_h$ by taking the zero-mean phase primitive of $F_h$. It is the scalar profile used in the leading pressure (3.3) and the construction of Lemma 3.1. Smoothness, period one and the identity $P_h'=F_h$ are established for $0<h\le1$; the definition alone does not supply those properties at arbitrary widths.
notes.TorusEuler.wavePrimaryPressure_hessian: For the constructed primitive, differentiating $-c(x)P_h(\phi(x))$ separates the rank-one term $-cF_h'(\phi)\nabla\phi\otimes\nabla\phi$ from terms involving derivatives of $c$ and curvature of $\phi$. With constant coefficient and linear phase, only the affine term in §1.2 remains. The formal formula allows variable $C^2$ coefficients and phase, but uses the specific profile family with $0<h\le1$.
notes.TorusEuler.wavePrimaryPressure_leading_u: For nonnegative $p_{\rm w}$, the leading pressure-Hessian term has quadratic form at most $(h/2)p_{\rm w}|k|^2|v|^2$. This gives (1.11) with $C=1/2$ for the constructed profile. The estimate controls the upper side of the Hessian, which is what the endpoint problem needs; it permits large negative curvature and also allows $p_{\rm w}=0$.
notes.TorusEuler.waveProfile: The velocity profile $F_h(s)$ is the integral of the normalized slope from zero to $s$, fixing $F_h(0)=0$. In Lemma 3.1, evenness and zero phase mean of that slope make the profile odd and periodic. Smoothness and the quantitative bounds are proved for the admissible range $0<h\le1$.
notes.TorusEuler.waveSlope: The slope is the periodized narrow bump minus its phase mean, divided by one minus that mean. This is the construction of $F_h'$ in §3.2 behind the profile properties introduced in §1.2. On $0<h\le1$, the normalization is valid and gives zero phase average, unit central value and a small negative part.
notes.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_one_of_activati: For positive growth rate $r$, the time cutoff equals one whenever $t\ge t_0+1/r$, including the endpoint. This is the condition $\tau\ge1$ in §6.2. The following crossing occurs later, so the full rank-one shear term is available when the next wave is activated.
notes.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_one_sub_envelop: The switch is exactly $\widetilde\chi(t)=1-\chi(1+r(t-t_0))$, using the cutoff fixed in §5.1. This identifies the smooth transition used in the formalization with the formula in §6.2. For positive $r$, its separate zero-before-activation property gives the same piecewise description as the paper.
notes.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_zero_of_le: For nonnegative growth rate, the time cutoff vanishes whenever $t\le t_0$, including at activation itself. Section 7 combines this with the zero initial data for higher oscillatory corrections to obtain $O_j=0$ on $[0,t_j]$. The cutoff identity alone concerns the leading switch, not the entire hierarchy.
notes.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_weighted_derivativ: If $|\gamma|\le G$ on the switching interval, then $|\widetilde\chi^{\prime}\gamma|\le CrG$ everywhere for one fixed constant $C$. The derivative vanishes outside that interval, so no global amplitude bound is needed. Section 6.2 applies this with the early-gain estimate (6.8) to make the switching contribution to the residual small.
notes.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forced_no: A nearby equation inherits the central weighted propagation estimate when its coefficient differs by at most the reciprocal of the central bound and the interval has length at most one. Variation of constants gives the factor $eK$ multiplying the initial weighted amplitude and the integral of the weighted forcing. Taking $K=\mathsf D^3$ gives (5.23).
notes.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forward: If the central homogeneous equation has weighted propagation bound $K$, a coefficient perturbation of size at most $K^{-1}$ changes that bound to $eK$ on an interval of length at most one. The weight is positive and differentiable. Applied with $K=\mathsf D^3$, this is the nearby-label Gronwall estimate used in the proof of Lemma 5.3.
